A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MMTEB research work, with complete main text and Appendices A–H. All 57 pages were compared, including text, equations, tables and graphics; no material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations in Table 2, benchmark optimization experiments in Appendix C, and English and code benchmark results in Tables 18–19.

after.justification: v4 retains the original empirical evaluations in Table 2, Appendix C and Tables 18–19, including measured performance, rankings and computational speedups.

M1.justification: The task-selection procedure, clustering subsampling, retrieval hard-negative sampling and embedding caching in Section 2.3 and Appendix C are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain identical dataset, language and task coverage, including the multilingual, European, Indic, English and code benchmarks. The task inventories in Appendices B, D and H are unchanged.

E2.justification: The experiment-specific model rosters in Tables 2, 18 and 19 and the optimization comparisons in Appendix C are identical. No evaluated comparator is added, removed or replaced.

E3.justification: Benchmark filtering, sample sizes, model configurations, evaluation metrics and aggregation procedures remain unchanged in Sections 2–3 and the appendices.

E4.justification: The synthetic-versus-gold retrieval comparison in Appendix B.3, clustering and retrieval downsampling analyses in Appendix C, and performance-by-language analyses are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Repeated-evaluation information, bootstrap distributions and significance analyses are unchanged. Appendix B.3 also retains the same reported 95% confidence interval for its rank correlation.

E6.justification: All reported experimental values, rankings and plotted findings match. For example, Table 2 retains multilingual-e5-large-instruct's 63.2 overall multilingual average, and Table 19 retains GritLM-7B's 73.6 code benchmark average.

T1.justification: The mathematical task-selection formulation in Section 2.3.3 and the abstention and normalized AUC definitions in Appendix F are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about benchmark coverage, computational efficiency and smaller multilingual models outperforming larger models in multilingual or low-resource settings.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning instruction tuning, pretraining language coverage and benchmark ranking differences remain identical. The limitations concerning English leakage, contributor credit and uneven language representation are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Dataset construction details, model revision IDs in Table 11, implementation and prompt references, and code and results access information are unchanged. The added contributor handle is an attribution update.

R1.justification: Section 5, the reference list and citations throughout the scientific text are unchanged. The relationship to MTEB, other embedding benchmarks and collaborative research projects is retained.

P1.justification: v4 adds Saksham Thakur to the title-page author list and Appendix A's author overview, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Research prose, terminology and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains a Saksham Thakur row, listing Sakshamrzt and Individual Contributor, slightly extending the table and shifting its caption. The title-page author line expands; scientific figures and result-table layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 updates author attribution on the title page and in Table 4, with minor accompanying layout changes. The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations and reproducibility information are unchanged, leaving overall paper quality materially equivalent.
